numerical_failure.observed_behavior: DatetimeArray/TimedeltaArray.isin with mismatched resolutions silently truncated the finer-resolution values when converting down (e.g. ns -> s), so values differing at sub-unit precision incorrectly matched and returned True
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: isin should return False for values that differ at nanosecond precision; both arrays should be cast up to the finer resolution via _ensure_matching_resos instead of lossy downcasting
trigger_conditions: self (DatetimeArray or TimedeltaArray) and values have mismatched resolutions
values have finer resolution than self (e.g. ns values checked against an s-unit array)
as_unit called with round_ok=True (the default) during isin, causing silent truncation when converting down
oracle_clues: Regression test test_isin_mismatched_reso in pandas/tests/arrays/test_datetimelike.py parametrized over (self_unit,val_unit) in [(s,ns),(ms,us),(us,ns),(ns,s)] and dtype_kind in [M,m]

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64 (M8) and timedelta64 (m8) arrays, DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray
numerical_characteristics.precision: Mismatched resolutions, e.g. seconds ('s') self vs nanoseconds ('ns') values; finer-resolution values are truncated when converted down to the coarser unit, and the reproducer's ns value 2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000001 differs from 2020-01-01 at nanosecond precision
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Values differing only at sub-unit precision (e.g. a 1 ns offset beyond a whole-second value); the regression test parametrizes resolution pairs (s,ns), (ms,us), (us,ns), (ns,s)
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: dta (unit 's') isin vals (unit 'ns') gives [True] before the fix (wrong) and [False] after (correct), since values differ at nanosecond precision.
Root cause per commit: isin called as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True (default), silently truncating finer-resolution values when converting down (ns -> s), causing false matches.
Fix: use _ensure_matching_resos, which casts both arrays up to the finer resolution with no information loss.

Test test_isin_mismatched_reso parametrized over dtype_kind in ['M','m'] and resolution pairs [('s','ns'),('ms','us'),('us','ns'),('ns','s')]; expected result for arr=[0,1] isin [1] is [False, False].
Whatsnew entry under Datetimelike for DatetimeArray.isin and TimedeltaArray.isin, issue GH64545.

Tolerance: no passage states a numeric or ULP tolerance; the 1-ULP tolerance question is unanswered by the evidence and the comparison is exact boolean match via tm.assert_numpy_array_equal, so tolerance is left null.
reproduction_risks: Using the default round_ok=True path hides the bug; a reproducer must pass values of mismatched resolution so truncation occurs.
Test comment references a placeholder GH#????? in one draft; the final issue number is 64545.
Passages give no numeric tolerance; comparison is exact boolean match via tm.assert_numpy_array_equal, not a floating tolerance.
Buggy commit hash 9bc2fcf7171b is given but no PR date is stated in the passages.
